2026-08-28T16:28:13.6279218Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6279605Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6279921Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6280407Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6280855Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6281343Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6282889Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6284556Z >
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6287408Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6289776Z >
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6290563Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6291310Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6291490Z ### How to Use
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6291727Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6292456Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6293171Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6293345Z ```bash
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6293892Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6294607Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6295213Z ```
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6295422Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6295958Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6296492Z ```bash
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6297052Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6297832Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6298661Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6299387Z ```
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6299596Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6300205Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6301059Z ```bash
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6301623Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6302291Z ```
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6302489Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6302801Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6303523Z ```bash
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6304040Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6304884Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6305794Z ```
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6306005Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6306269Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6306677Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6308056Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6309580Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6309743Z ```bash
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6310185Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6311021Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6311814Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6312127Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6312599Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6313583Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6314376Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6314844Z ```
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6315046Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6315950Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6316836Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6317005Z ```bash
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6317672Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6318549Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6319257Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6319676Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6320071Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6320857Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6321400Z ```
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6321610Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6321813Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6322611Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6323558Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6324502Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6325653Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6326736Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6327295Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6327478Z ### Notes
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6327693Z 
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6328302Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6329688Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6330907Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6332118Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6333296Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6334380Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6335329Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-28T16:28:13.6336195Z </mcp-clis>
